sensors.name: line tracker brightness in % (LINETRACKER, LIGHT mode)

control_flow: driveInTheDark: if the line tracker reads under 70 % (black line), drive straight forward at 40 %; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Drive through a tunnel and come out the other side.

decision_points.condition: the line tracker reads less than 70 % (a black line under it)

branches.outcome: black: it drives straight forward at 40 %
not black: it checks the obstacle sensor
an obstacle is ahead: it stops
nothing is ahead: it follows the line

branches.reason: On black the line tracker reads under 50 %, so the first check already drove forward; this branch can never run.
branches.outcome: black: it curves left (left wheel 10 %, right 40 %)
no black: it curves right (left wheel 40 %, right 10 %)

equivalence_classes: a black line under it all the way
input_dimensions.dimension: what the line tracker sees while the robot is in the tunnel

equivalence_classes: a wall within reach of the obstacle sensor
input_dimensions.dimension: what is in front of the robot when it is off the line
what the line tracker sees when the robot is off the line

scenarios.coded_response: The line tracker reads black (under 70 %), so it drives straight forward at 40 %, again and again.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot stands on a black line that runs straight through a tunnel, facing along it, with nothing in front of it.
scenarios.title: Drives through the tunnel along the line
assumptions: A black line runs through the tunnel and along it the robot drives.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It drives through the tunnel and out the other side.

scenarios.coded_response: The line tracker reads the peach floor (not black), the obstacle sensor sees a wall ahead, and it stops.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot stands on the open floor, off any line, with a wall right in front of it.
scenarios.trigger: The obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops in front of a wall
assumptions: You didn't say what it should do at a wall; the program stops there and that part is called stopAtWall.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops in front of the wall without bumping into it.

scenarios.coded_response: It checks the obstacle sensor, sees nothing, and curves right (left wheel 40 %, right wheel 10 %).
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot stands on the open floor, off any line, with nothing in front of it.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker doesn't see black.
scenarios.title: Off the line it curves right

uncertainties: The line tracker's light % is the floor's brightness, not the room's: inside a tunnel it still reads black on the line and 83 % on the floor, so the tunnel's darkness changes nothing the program does.
You didn't say how the robot should find its way through the tunnel; the program drives straight only while the line tracker is on black.
The check 'sees black' in followLine can never be true: the first check already drove forward whenever the line is black.

planned: Drives through the tunnel to the other side

outcomes.words: the condition doesn't hold: the else part runs
planned: Stands still with a wall ahead

outcomes.words: the condition doesn't hold: the else part runs

outcomes.deferred: On black the line tracker reads under 50 %, so the first check already drove forward; this branch can never run.

tests.name: Drives through the tunnel to the other side
tests.scenario: Given the robot starts on a black line 15 cm before a straight tunnel, and the line runs straight through it, when the program runs, then the robot drives through the tunnel and reaches Goal 1 just beyond its exit without bumping into the tunnel's walls.

equivalence_partitions.selected_realization: the line t2 runs under the robot from A and straight through the tunnel t1
equivalence_partitions.dimension: what the line tracker sees while the robot is in the tunnel
equivalence_partitions.class: a black line under it all the way

expected_results: It drives straight along the line, through the tunnel, and reaches Goal 1 beyond the exit.

postconditions.description: By the end of the run, the robot has touched Goal 1 after the tunnel.
During the whole run, it never bumps into the tunnel's walls.

assumptions: The tunnel is straight and a black line runs through it, so your program can drive straight on.

tests.reason: You said the robot should get through the tunnel, and on a black line it drives straight forward.

tests.name: Stands still with a wall ahead
tests.scenario: Given the robot stands off the line with a wall 8 cm in front of it, when the program runs for 5 s, then it stays still and does not drive into the wall.

equivalence_partitions.selected_realization: the Wall t2, 8 cm in front of A, so the obstacle sensor sees it at once
equivalence_partitions.dimension: what is in front of the robot when it is off the line
equivalence_partitions.class: a wall within reach of the obstacle sensor

expected_results: It stays still in front of the wall instead of driving into it.

postconditions.description: During the whole run, the robot never bumps into the wall.
From 0.1 s to the end of the run, the robot stands still.

assumptions: You didn't say what the robot should do at a wall; your program stops there, so the test expects it to stop.

tests.reason: It shows that the robot stays in front of a wall instead of driving into it.
